requirements.text: The solution should provide detailed context-sensitive help material for all the possible actions and scenarios on all user interfaces in the application.
The help should be accessible to the users both in the offline and online mode
The solution should provide an interface for the user to log any defects or enhancement requests on the application and track thereafter.
The solution should send alerts (e.g., email, SMS) to the user if the user chooses to whenever any action has been taken on the alert
The solution should enable the user to track the submitted defect or enhancement request.
The solution should enable the help-desk user to view the reports on the submitted defects or enhancement requests category-wise, status-wise, and age-wise.
The support solution should be accessible to the users both from within the application and also outside the application through a browser interface.

The System must keep an unalterable audit trail capable of automatically capturing and storing information about: All the actions (create/read/update/delete) that are taken upon the critical entities (case, suspect, property,…) in the system; The user initiating and or carrying out the action; The date and time of the event.
Once the audit trail functionality has been activated, the System must track events without manual intervention, and store in the audit trail information about them.
The System must maintain the audit trail for as long as required, which will be at least for the life of the case to which it refers.

The System must ensure that audit trail data is available for inspection on request, so that a specific event can be identified and all related data made accessible, and that this can be achieved by authorised external personnel who have little or no familiarity with the system.
The System must be able to export audit trails for specified cases (without affecting the audit trail stored by the System).

The System must be able to capture and store violations (i.e. A user’s attempts to access a case to which he is denied access), and (where violations can validly be attempted) attempted violations, of access control mechanisms.
The System must at a minimum be able to provide reports for actions on cases organised: By case; By user; In chronological sequence.
The System should be able to provide reports for actions on cases organised by workstation and (where technically appropriate) by network address.
The System must allow the user to limit access to cases to specified users or user groups.
The system should provide for role-based control for the functionality within the system.
The System must allow a user to be a member of more than one group.
The System must allow only admin-users to set up user profiles and allocate users to groups.
The System should allow a user to stipulate which other users or groups can access cases.
The System must allow changes to security attributes for groups or users (such as access rights, security level, privileges, password allocation and management) to be made only by super-user.
If a user performs a quick or advanced search, the System must never include in the search result list any record which the user does not have the right to access.
If the System allows users to make unauthorised attempts to access cases, it must log these in the audit trail.

Any access to cases, and all other activities involving the cases and related documents or data should also need to be stored in the audit trail to ensure legal admissibility and to assist in data recovery.
The system should support multilingual interface
The system should be designed in manner that operational data is not lost in case of any failure of equipment or communication network.
The system should work even in an offline mode with the critical functionality
The system should be designed to have satisfactory performance even in Police Stations connected on low-bandwidth
The system should be implemented using Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) and have a modular design
The system should be developed on Open Standards
The system should be built on a common User Access and Authentication Service to ensure Single-Sign on for the end-user
The system should be developed for a centralized deployment and maintenance
The system should be developed to be deployed in a 3-tier datacenter architecture
The system should be designed to have a n-tier architecture with the presentation logic separated from the business logic that is again separated from the data-access logic
The system should be extensible to provide access to the interfaces through PDA’s and mobile data terminals
The system should adopt standardized formats and common metadata elements
The system should be designed for access through browser-based systems and must impose minimal requirements on the client device
The system must support multiple types of communication services for remote access
The system should have capability to support public access to a subset of data and functionality
The system should support multi-tier authentication where required
The system should support SSL encrypted connections
The system should support secure virtual private network connections
The system should use HTTPS as the communication protocol, i.e., HTTP over an encrypted secure socket layer (SSL)
The system should run on multiple browsers
The system should support selective encryption of the stored data
The system should ensure secure transmission of data over the network and utilize SSL and 2-way digital signatures
The system must enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all administrative accounts and for all remote access sessions, utilizing at least two independent authentication factors.
The system must encrypt all Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and sensitive criminal records at rest using AES-256 or higher encryption standards.
The system must utilize IPsec or TLS 1.3 based VPN tunnels with FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules for all remote connections.
The system must maintain 99.9% availability during operational hours, with a maximum allowable unplanned downtime of 4 hours per quarter.
In the event of any software or hardware failure, the system must be restored to full operational status within 4 hours.
The system must support offline data entry with a deterministic 'last-write-wins' or 'version-vector' based reconciliation strategy upon reconnection to ensure data integrity.
The system must maintain a page load time of under 5 seconds for critical modules when operating on a network connection with a bandwidth of 128 kbps and 300ms latency.
The system must ensure that 95% of all page requests are rendered within 3 seconds under standard network conditions (1 Mbps).
The system must achieve 99.9% uptime during operational hours, with planned maintenance windows restricted to Sunday 00:00 to 04:00 local time.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify password complexity, rotation, or account lockout policies for the authentication service. - The system must enforce a password policy requiring a minimum of 12 characters, including complexity requirements, and implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts.

OPEN: The PRD lacks defined load parameters (e.g., concurrent users, total records) to validate the performance requirements. - The system must support 50,000 concurrent users and a database growth of 10 million records per year while maintaining the specified search response times.

OPEN: The PRD lacks defined concurrency requirements, such as the number of concurrent users or total registered users, which are essential for sizing the 3-tier datacenter architecture. - The system must support a minimum of 50,000 concurrent users across all state-level deployments with a peak load capacity of 100,000 concurrent sessions.
The system shall manage customer accounts.
The system shall manage an online store inventory.
The system shall manage a customer’s “Shopping Cart”.
The system shall confirm orders.
The system shall have an unambiguous interface to assist in browsing the categories and products.
The system shall use Secure Socket Layer (SSL) for security.
The system shall have an availability of 99.999%.
The system shall allow an optional mirror site for reliability and backups.
The system shall feature an interface for future software enhancement via “Plug-ins”.
Customers will be able to create accounts to store their customer profiles, configure contact information, view their purchase history, and confirm orders.
Customers will be able to register, log in, and log out of their accounts.
The inventory management will allow for administrators to update the categories, the products placed in categories, and the specific product details.
The shopping cart will clearly display the number of items in the cart, along with the total cost.
The customer will be able to add to or remove products from the shopping cart prior to checkout and order confirmation.
If the order is incorrect, the customer will be able to revise and update their order.
The customer will then receive a confirmation email with the specific order details.
The system will implement an Application Interface to allow for various plug-ins to interact with the system.
The WebOrder system shall send an e-mail confirmation to the customer that the items they ordered will be delivered to the shipping address along with tracking number.
The WebOrder system shall send an e-mail to System Administrator regarding any technical queries from customers or sales people.

The system shall enforce a minimum password length of 12 characters, require a mix of alphanumeric and special characters, and store passwords using a salted, slow hashing algorithm (e.g., Argon2 or bcrypt).

The system shall not store full Primary Account Numbers (PAN) in the database; if storage is required, it must be PCI-DSS compliant, using tokenization or strong encryption at rest with restricted access.
The system shall integrate with a PCI-compliant payment gateway to process transactions, ensuring no sensitive card data is processed or stored directly by the Web Store application.
The system shall maintain 99.999% availability, measured as uptime over a rolling 12-month period, excluding scheduled maintenance windows of no more than 1 hour per month.

The system shall provide a sandboxed execution environment for plug-ins, ensuring that a plug-in failure cannot terminate the core Web Store process, and shall implement versioning for all API endpoints.
Define a maximum page load time (e.g., 'The system shall render the product catalog page in under 2 seconds for 95% of requests').
Specify the record size and the database state (e.g., 'The system shall restore 1000 records of 1KB each per second from a cold backup').
Define the retrieval criteria (e.g., 'The system shall retrieve 200 products per second from the database under a load of 1000 concurrent users').

OPEN: The plug-in API lacks defined security boundaries or sandboxing requirements, which could allow malicious plug-ins to compromise the entire system. - The system shall execute third-party plug-ins within a restricted, sandboxed environment with limited access to the underlying OS, database, and network resources.

OPEN: The PRD mentions an optional mirror site for reliability but does not define the failover mechanism, synchronization latency, or the recovery point objective (RPO). - The system shall support a secondary mirror site with a maximum data synchronization latency of 5 seconds and an automated failover mechanism that triggers within 30 seconds of primary node failure.

OPEN: The PRD specifies a 4GB Flash RAM chip but does not define the durability or write-cycle limitations for a system that logs transactions and updates inventory on a USB device. - The system shall implement wear-leveling and log rotation policies to ensure the storage medium remains functional for a minimum of 3 years under expected transaction volumes.

OPEN: The PRD specifies a requirement for 1000 concurrent customers but does not define the expected average or peak transaction volume per customer, making it impossible to size the hardware (Intel XScale PXA270) correctly. - Define the expected transactions per second (TPS) or requests per second (RPS) the system must support under the 1000 concurrent user load.
XML Services shall be segmented.
The XS shall have the ability to redefine or reset names of connect descriptors to database server instances.
At a minimum, the session time-out values shall be user definable and be able to be reset prior to initialization of a user session.
The data management services shall support managing various types of data, database architectures and platforms that includes hardware and software at the specified sites.
The Registry shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix B .
The XS function shall provide standard APIs as specified in Appendix C .
The XS shall internally interface (transparent to the operator) with the existing data elements of the DBIF, DAC, and COTS RDBMS products.
The Registry software shall be portable and required to execute on COE-compliant platforms.
The XS software shall be delivered in accordance with DII COE guidelines.

Manager services shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) and maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, including user creation, privilege escalation, and configuration changes.
Maintenance operations involving modification of user permissions and privileges shall require multi-factor authentication and dual-authorization (two-person integrity) for production environments.

XML Services shall be architected into independent, failure-isolated segments such that a failure in one segment (e.g., Registry) does not prevent the operation of other segments (e.g., Producer/Consumer services).
The Registry software shall be portable across all COE-compliant platforms, defined as [List of OS/Hardware architectures], and shall not rely on platform-specific kernel extensions.
Upon session time-out, the XS shall perform a graceful rollback of uncommitted transactions and release all held database locks to prevent resource exhaustion.
Define specific latency requirements for XML document generation/parsing (e.g., 'process 1MB XML document in < 500ms') and throughput requirements for registry queries.
Define the specific network performance metrics (e.g., latency in ms, packet loss percentage) that trigger an automatic or manual adjustment of session time-outs.

OPEN: The PRD mentions Discretionary Access Control (DAC) in the glossary but fails to define the security policy or enforcement mechanism for the XML Registry. - The XML Registry shall enforce Mandatory Access Control (MAC) and Discretionary Access Control (DAC) policies consistent with the DII COE security architecture for all metadata and schema objects.

OPEN: The PRD mentions the use of FTP and email for submitting Information Resource Packages but does not specify security requirements for data in transit. - All Information Resource Submittal Packages transmitted via email or FTP shall be encrypted using FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules to ensure confidentiality and integrity.

OPEN: The requirement for managing 'various types of data, database architectures and platforms' is too broad to ensure system stability or maintainability. - The data management services shall support [List of specific RDBMS versions and hardware platforms] to ensure consistent behavior and predictable failure modes.

OPEN: There is no definition of expected database sizes, number of concurrent users, or registry entry volume, which are critical for scaling the XML Services architecture. - Include capacity requirements specifying the maximum number of concurrent sessions, total registry entries, and expected database record counts.
